page: The Vultr voc-c-1c-2gb-25s-amd is an entry-level compute-optimized instance from the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features a single dedicated physical core and single thread based on the x86_64 AMD EPYC processor platform clocked at 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside support for advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16. Hardware resources include 2.0 GB of system memory, bundled local storage comprising a 25 GB NVMe SSD, and one complimentary public IPv4 address without discrete GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations reveal strong single-threaded processing capabilities alongside the expected throughput limits of a single-core environment. The instance achieved a top-tier stress-ng single-core score of 3373.08, complemented by robust performance in single-threaded compression benchmarks, registering 31.6 GB/sec in gzip and 14.2 GB/sec in bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate multi-threaded capabilities and total throughput reflect its single-core ceiling, yielding a multi-core stress-ng result of 3373.08 and a PassMark CPU score of 2955.8. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 35.29 GB/sec, while write operations measured 32.48 GB/sec.

The 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides an efficient compute-leaning profile for tasks requiring dedicated processor time without excessive memory overhead. The inclusion of dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent processing execution compared to shared or burstable alternatives. Workload suitability centers on lightweight compute tasks, dedicated background utility workers, microservices, small automated scripts, CI build runners, and single-threaded data compression tasks.
